image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a cluster of ripe, dark purple figs on a white background. The figs exhibit a glossy, wrinkled skin texture with deep red and purple hues. Several figs show their stems (pedicels) attached, appearing greenish-brown. One central fig clearly displays the ostiole (the small opening at the bottom). The lighting creates strong specular highlights on the smooth skin surfaces.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The skin exhibits an overly uniform, plastic-like glossiness. While real figs can be shiny, the highlights here appear slightly synthetic and lack the subtle micro-texture variations of natural fruit skin, suggesting mild AI smoothing or over-sharpening.

artifact_observations.location: Stem attachment points on peripheral figs
artifact_observations.reasoning: The stems on the figs at the far left and bottom edges appear to merge into the fruit body without a clear, distinct junction. The geometry becomes ambiguous, looking more like a protrusion of the fruit skin than a separate attached stem structure.
